title: Watch Jobs
markdown:
The **watch** module (`openexecutive.watch`) runs **watch jobs**: unattended ERPNext runs, defined in code, that read a fixed set of ERPNext data, apply rules in code and leave notices and draft cards. A job never runs the Executive's tool loop, never lets a model choose a read, and never writes a figure or a card's field a model made up: a model writes only short reason lines. Six jobs are listed: **collections** (who to chase today, and the payment reminders due), **payment checks** (a likely duplicate supplier invoice held before it's paid, and a changed bank account flagged for a phone call), **quote follow-up** (the quotations about to lapse, and those lapsed this week with no order, each with a call to make on a ToDo card), **bank matching** (a bank line ERPNext's own rules left unreconciled, matched with the one submitted voucher it most likely is, on a card the reviewer approves), **invoice capture** (a supplier's mailed invoice filled from the one order or receipt its PDF clearly bills, on a card the draft's assignee approves) and **late deliveries** (the open purchase orders past their date, worst first, each with the supplier's delivery record and a chase note on a ToDo card for the buyer).

### The registry (`watch.registry`), code only

- A job is a `WatchJob(id, title, reads, build, schedule, card_cap_day, default_settings, reason_schema=None, check_fields=None, setting_bounds={}, card_noun="drafts", slots=(), weekdays=all, extra_notices=None, once=False)`. Its id is oe_connector's `[a-z0-9-]{1,40}`, the key of the job's listing in `oe_connector_watch_jobs` and of its ERP user `oe-watch-<id>@<site>`.
- `reads` is a tuple of `WatchRead(tool, shape, arguments, label)`: an oe_connector tool, the shape of its arguments as oe_connector lists it (a literal matches only the same JSON type and value, so `true` is never `1` and `1.0` never `1`; a slot `$company`, `$date` (an ISO date within 400 days), `$party`, `$parties` / `$customers` (up to 50 names), `$int` (1–500), `$bank_line` (a Bank Transaction; oe_connector also checks it is on an account listed for bank matching), `$mail_draft` and `$mail_file` (a mailed draft Purchase Invoice and its mail's one file, by name; sound only together as a `read_attachment` read's top-level `name` and `file` beside `"doctype": "Purchase Invoice"`, never on another tool, nested, in a filter or in a list; oe_connector checks the pair against its own mail-capture rules) takes any value of its type, and `$bank_account` is this side's own slot (`LOCAL_SLOTS`) for a value oe_connector's listing holds as a literal, one read per account; the top-level `fields` list is the most a call may ask for; any other list matches a list of the same length element by element, such as `["<=", "$date"]` or `["in", "$parties"]`, never "any list"; an object has exactly its keys), the code that builds the run's arguments, and how a notice names it.
- **Repeated reads.** A read with `repeat` (1–50, `MAX_REPEAT`) makes one call per item (with `may_fail`, one item ERPNext refuses, such as an unreadable PDF, becomes `{"unread": true}` instead of ending the run; the job's rules never make a card of it): its `arguments` return `Repeated(arguments, truncated)`, and the runner makes at most `repeat` of them, recording any more as `truncated`. Each call has its own shape check, read marker, timeout and `acting` record; `build` gets `{"each": [results], "truncated": bool}`, and a refused call ends the run as any read's would. Bank matching reads each listed account's lines this way, then each line's candidates.
- **Dependent reads.** `arguments(settings, today, prior)` gets the earlier reads' results (their `acting` removed). A derived list that comes out empty returns `None`: the read is **skipped**, never sent with an empty list, `build` gets `{}` for it, and the run records `{"read", "skipped": true}`. A list cut to its first 50 by the job's own order comes back as `Derived(arguments, truncated=True)`, recorded `truncated`. A derived argument is shape-checked like any other before the call, and oe_connector checks it again as the job's user.
- **Sound shapes only** (oe_connector's own rules, ladislav-urban/oe_connector#536): a `$` string that isn't a slot, a list or object inside a list, a slot in a list anywhere but `[operator, slot]` (`= != < <= > >=` before a single-value slot, `in` / `not in` before `$parties` or `$customers` only), or a list slot as a filter's value on its own makes a read unsound, and `WatchJob` refuses the job when it is defined. Both checkers are tested against oe_connector's own `watch_shape_vectors.json` (its soundness cases, its match cases and their slot oracle).
- **Slots.** A job runs once a day at `schedule`, or at each of its `slots` (times, in order, the first its schedule) on its `weekdays`.
- Any job may list `run_report` and `list_records`. A tool the gateway withholds from every turn (`connected_systems.ERPNEXT_WITHHELD_TOOLS`) may be listed only by the job `JOB_WITHHELD_EXCEPTIONS` gives it to: `customer_payment_record` by collections alone, `supplier_bank_changed` by payment checks alone (chat never reads it, whoever asks), `bank_lines_to_match` and `bank_line_candidates` by bank matching alone. `mail_invoices_to_fill` is pinned and withheld with no job yet. `WatchJob.__post_init__` refuses any other listing, so the registry mirrors the gateway's one exception.
- `build(results, settings, today)` is pure code returning notices (`CardSpec(key, summary, values, facts, items, notes, count)`: `items` are its rows, each a finding of its own for the reason step; `notes` are lines in code's own words) and draft cards (`DraftSpec(key, operation, doctype, fields, expect, title, reason_key, group, name, notice)`: `name` is the document a change or a block is on, `notice` the finding told as a notice when no card can be left for it). `check_fields(operation, doctype, fields, name)` is the job's own builder of a card's fields; it runs before each check and again at approval, so a tampered card is refused.
- Settings are exactly the job's `default_settings` keys and types; a whole number is 1–500 unless `setting_bounds` gives it others (collections' `min_amount` 0 up to a billion, bank matching's `amount_cap_day` 1 to 1,000,000), and a list holds 0–50 names unless `setting_bounds` gives its count others (bank matching's `bank_accounts` at most 10). A job's `extra_notices(settings, day)` adds notices from this install's own records after `build` (bank matching's monthly list of the matches made, and of those whose result ERPNext never confirmed, left for the principal: never for the reviewer who approved them).
- **Once, not daily** (`once`): a job whose findings are each raised once, ever (quote follow-up's, once per quotation and state; late deliveries', once per order and ISO week, the week being part of the finding's key). When a notice of such a job is left, the runner records what it told (its key, its rows' keys and `CardSpec.counted`, the findings it counts without naming) as dedupe digests in `watch_told (job, key, day)` (`settings.mark_told`, forgotten after 400 days); the job's rules read them back (`runner.told`, a failed read ends the run rather than tell everything again) and leave those findings out. Cards dedupe apart from the notice: a told finding still gets its card on a later day when the day's cap or the reviewer's room held it back, and a finding gets no second card while one waits for the current reviewer and is still the job's own, while one is being approved, or once an approval was tried at all, went unanswered (its final `no_answer`), or a person approved or dismissed one. A card never tried that expired, or that code closed or would now refuse (the assignee or reviewer changed, a configurer refusal), is closed (from waiting only: one an approval claimed meanwhile holds) and its finding gets a new card on the next run while it's due. A finding the ledger's 5,000-card listing no longer shows is held by its `card:<digest>` row in `watch_told`, dropped when its card is seen expired or code-closed. A once job's finding is told on its own only when ERPNext kept its card from the reviewer: its row comes off the reviewer's notice, and it goes to the principal, once. A notice that fails to store records nothing, so its findings are told on the next run.
- `JOBS` is read-only and holds only what the module lists (`_LISTED`: collections, payment checks, bank matching, invoice capture, quote follow-up and late deliveries). Nothing adds a job from settings, chat or an API; the test job `watch.jobs._example` is put in by the tests. `tests/unit/watch_job_vectors.json` pins the id pattern, slot names, shapes, phase 1's jobs' reads and one signed `watch` assertion against oe_connector; `watch_shape_vectors.json` mirrors oe_connector's own shape cases, `$bank_line`'s included.

### Settings (`watch.settings`, table `watch_jobs`)

One row per job: `enabled` (off by default), `settings` (JSON, checked as above), `configured_by_person_id` and `configured_at`, and an optional `reviewer_person_id`: the person the job's notices and draft cards go to, when the run's routing allows (below). Only the principal changes a row, through `PUT /watch/jobs/{id}` (a signed principal or local login's operator; see API Reference), which records who did it and writes a private `watch_job_configured` audit row. The reviewer must be an active team member who is neither the principal (who configures every job, and never approves its cards) nor a demo person: 400 otherwise. `GET /watch/jobs` carries `reviewer_note`, what Settings says beside the reviewer: they see the job's notices, with the figures ERPNext read as the job's own user, and approve its cards. No chat action calls either route. `ERPNEXT_WATCH_JOBS_ENABLED` (off) is the operator's master switch: off, no job runs whatever its row says.

### The read marker and the gateway

Each read runs inside `erpnext_caller.watch_run(job, tool, arguments)`, a marker code sets and no tool can. It is bound to a job that is registered and on, one of the tools it lists, and the digest of the call's exact arguments, which must fit the read's shape. It is refused (`WatchRefused`, a reason code) while a turn's session is bound, while any other marker is set (the brief's, the oversight export's, the answer check's, a supplier's, a draft's or a job's check, or another watch read's), and without `ERPNEXT_CALLER_PRIVATE_KEY` (`watch-needs-keys`). It saves the marker it found and puts it back on exit.

Inside it `caller_for` answers `ErpnextCaller("watch", job=<id>)` before any session logic, and only alone. `mint` signs `kind: "watch"` with `sub` the job's id, never a `purpose`, and refuses any draft tool. The gateway refuses every other call inside the marker (`outside-watch-read`), compares the arguments' digest after its own argument coercion, and re-checks at call time that no turn and no other marker is bound. A withheld tool is refused on every path but one (`mcp_gateway._job_reads_withheld`): inside `watch_run`, with exactly that tool bound, for the job `JOB_WITHHELD_EXCEPTIONS` gives it to, with no turn and no other marker. Chat, ERPNext's panel, the brief, a supplier's agent, every draft marker and any other job's read are still refused, and tool search never shows it.

oe_connector checks the job is listed and the call fits one of its listed reads, as the job's own narrow ERP user when the job is set `as_job_user`, else the OE Reader service view, and reports which in the result's top-level `acting` (`{kind, job, as_job_user, user}`). The runner reads only that top-level key: per read, whether it ran as exactly `oe-watch-<job>@<site>`, the same user on every read; `acting.job` naming another job ends the run.

### The job's check marker (`draft_check_for_job`)

A job's draft card is checked by ERPNext **as the job's reviewer**, so its summary and fingerprint are what the reviewer can see, and approval later runs as the same person. `erpnext_caller.draft_check_for_job(job, arguments, email, person_id=, day=)` marks the one `erpnext__draft_check` call (`DraftCall.unattended`, with the job and the reviewer's person id), signed `kind: "user"`, `purpose: "draft"` as the reviewer. It is refused (`JobCheckRefused`, a code) under a turn's session or any other marker (a watch read's included: it never nests, and no draft marker can be set inside it), without the caller key, for a job that isn't registered and on, unless the arguments are `{operation, doctype, [name,] fields}` with the fields exactly as the job's `check_fields` builds them (`draft_check` takes nothing else, so never `asked_by` or `configured_by`), unless the person is the job's current reviewer under that email (active, on the team, not a demo person, not the principal), and past the day's cap (two runs' worth of `card_cap_day` checks plus 2 retries, counted in `watch_days.checks`, so a restart never resets it and a refused check still counts). The gateway refuses any other tool under it (`outside-job-check`), refuses it under a session or a watch read, and reads the reviewer again from People and the job's row when it signs.

### The runner (`watch.runner`)

- **Once a day, or at each slot.** A scheduler tick hook (`maybe_run`) starts each job that is on, on its weekdays, once one of its slots is due in the company's time zone (collections at 07:00, before the brief; late deliveries at 07:15 and quote follow-up at 07:30, Monday to Friday; payment checks hourly 08:00–18:00, Monday to Friday), when it wins that slot's claim: a `watch_runs` row keyed `(job, day, slot)` (`slot` "HH:MM", "" for a daily job; `status`, `started_at`, `attempts`, `cards`, `error`, `reads`, `detail`) taken under `BEGIN IMMEDIATE`. Only the latest due slot is claimed: earlier ones with no row are marked `skipped` in the same transaction, so a worker down for three hours runs once, not three times. A run left `running` for 30 minutes is retried once while its slot is still the latest due, then failed; one a later slot has overtaken is failed (`run_overtaken`), never retried, and a later slot waits while an earlier run is still fresh. A day whose hour daylight saving skipped still runs. A `watch_runs` table from before slots is migrated once, its rows kept with slot "". `watch_days (job, day, cards, failure_noticed, amount, checks, notices)` counts the day's draft cards, the amount of the match cards left, the checks made as the reviewer and the notices tried (at most `card_cap_day` a day, however many slots), each in one transaction across slots, workers and restarts, and lets a job leave one failure notice a calendar day. `watch_approved (job, day, person_id, decision_id, amount)` counts what was approved of a job's amount-capped cards that day, by anyone, one row per card (the approver kept for the audit). Each run is one task of its own, with no session and no audit scope, under the turn id `watch:<id>:<day>` and the job's cost budget once cost caps are in.
- **Reads.** Each read's arguments are built by the job's code (skipped or truncated as above) and checked against its shape before the call. A refused or failed read ends the run: the principal gets one notice a day naming the read and why, in our words, and nothing partial is raised. A refusal naming `oe_connector_bank_facts` (ladislav-urban/oe_connector#534) says "Supplier bank checks are off in ERPNext's settings." The run's row, the log and the audit hold a reason code only, never ERPNext's text.
- **Rules.** `job.build` turns the results into notices and draft cards. At most 200 findings a run.
- **Routing** (`watch.cards.route`), from the database and oe_connector's own word, never a model or a read's result. The run goes to the job's reviewer only when every read made (at least one; a skipped read counts neither way) ran as the job's own user, the reviewer's People row is active, on the team, not a demo person, not the principal, not whoever configured the job, and has an email, and teammates' drafts (`ERPNEXT_DRAFTS_TEAMMATES`) and signed sign-ins are on. Otherwise the principal gets the notices only, and the run records why (`detail.routed_principal`: `no_reads`, `not_job_user`, `no_reviewer`, `reviewer_unavailable`, `reviewer_is_configurer`, `teammates_off`, `signing_off`).
- **Reasons** (a job with a `reason_schema`): one tool-less call to the fast utility model with its own constant system prompt (`REASON_SYSTEM`), shown the notices' rows (each finding's bounded facts, at most 20) wrapped as untrusted and keyed by short ids. Only a JSON object of reasons for the ids it was shown is kept, each cleaned and at most 200 characters. A reason is labelled as a model's words, never as a figure, and never reaches a key, a title, a card's fields or routing.
- **Cards** (`watch.cards.leave_drafts`), only once routing named the reviewer: no check is ever made for a run that went to the principal. A kind of card that is off on this server (a DocType not listed for drafts or changes, a block while any of its three switches is off, a bank match while `ERPNEXT_BANK_MATCH` or its pin is off) isn't proposed. For each `DraftSpec` in the job's order: none while the same finding's card waits or once one was left that day; at most `card_cap_day` a day, across the day's slots (taken before the check, given back when no card is left); at most 10 of the job's cards waiting; and never the reviewer past `OPEN_CARDS_MAX` less 5, so their own asks still fit. ERPNext checks each card as the reviewer under the check marker; the check must read back the card the job built (a new draft: the operation, the DocType and what the job expects, as collections' invoice, customer and company; a change: the same document and change, and a draft that is the reviewer's own or assigned to them; a block: that invoice, the one it repeats, the card's release date, its supplier and company; a bank match: `erpnext_match`'s reading, below) and give a fingerprint, or no card is left. A bank match must also fit what is left of the job's `amount_cap_day` for the day's cards (taken in a transaction, given back when no card is left). Some refusals are our own reading of ERPNext's answer and get their own line in the notice (another currency, not the whole line, a reviewer ERPNext names as the importer or a voucher's creator, the day's amount). A finding with no card is told as its notice, when the job gave one. Each check writes a private `watch_job_check` audit row (job, day, operation, person id, a result code, never ERPNext's text). A refused check leaves no card, and the notice says how many in code's words ("… couldn't be prepared as <reviewer>: their ERPNext access doesn't allow it"). When every check of a run was refused for the reviewer's permissions, the run's notice goes to the principal. Every job card signs `configured_by`, who set the job up here; ERPNext checks it against the configurer the site records for the job (`oe_connector_watch_jobs[job].configured_by`, set by the ERPNext operator), and a card naming someone else, or a job with none recorded, is refused and closed (`configurer_not_recorded`), never retried. A finding ERPNext kept from the reviewer (their permissions, or separation of duties) is told to the principal as its notice, never back to the reviewer (`CardSpec.to_principal`).
- **Notices.** Private alerts (source `watch`, `needs: fyi`) stored directly, never through triage: routed as above. The headline is code only (the job's title and counts); every ERPNext string in the body is stripped and capped, the body is wrapped `wrap_untrusted(source="erpnext", author="watch:<id>")`, each row is shown with its reason ("Why now", a model's words), and code's own lines follow the block: the job's notes, how many cards wait for whom, and why none were prepared ("Name a reviewer in Settings → Watch jobs to get the reminder drafts."). A finding whose notice is still open isn't raised again, nor one already raised that day; a `once` job's finding, never again.
- **Audit.** One private `watch_run` row per run: status, reason code and counts (notices, cards left, repeats, capped, checks, refused), who it went to; never ERPNext's figures or text.

### Job draft cards and separation of duties (`integrations.erpnext_drafts`)

- **Left in code**, never through `propose_erpnext_draft` or triage: `leave_job_card` goes through the same `propose` as every card (the digest dedupe, a new fingerprint replacing the waiting card, never a card changed in place), scoped to the job so a person's own chat card is never one of them, with `source: "watch"`, `job`, `run_day`, `asked_by` (the reviewer's email the check ran as), `asked_by_person_id`, `approver_person_id` (the reviewer), `configured_by_person_id` (who configured the job when the run left it), the finding's `dedup_key` and the reason line. Its headline is code's; the card shows the job's title ("Dunning draft from the Collections job") and the reason as "Why now: …".
- **Approval** (`_job_approval`, before anything is claimed), besides every card's own checks: **separation of duties first, whatever `ERPNEXT_DRAFT_SOD` says**: the approver is neither the card's configurer nor the job's current one, and the configurer's People row still exists, is active and has an email; otherwise "You set up this job, so someone else approves its cards. Nothing was made." and the card closes as `sod_refused`, audited (`erpnext_draft_sod_refused`). Then the job is registered and on (master switch and row), the approver is not the principal or a demo person, is the card's stored approver and the job's current reviewer, the fields are exactly what the job's `check_fields` builds (a Dunning with its letter date), and the fingerprint is there.
- **The wire values** come from the stored keys, never a model: the write tool gets `asked_by: "job:<id>"` and `configured_by`, the configurer's **current** People email, resolved at approval, with `expected_fingerprint`. `draft_check` never gets either. oe_connector applies its own separation of duties when the site's `oe_connector_draft_sod` is `agent`; its refusal closes the card the same way.

### Collections (`watch.jobs.collections`)

- **Reads**, as listed in oe_connector: Accounts Receivable by due date for the company on the day (up to 500 rows); the Dunnings sent (submitted, with customer, date, type and the invoices each covered) and those still in draft (up to 500 each); and `customer_payment_record` for the overdue customers, the 50 largest by amount × days, derived from the first read (skipped when nobody is overdue).
- **Rules** (code, tested on fixed data): who to chase, in order: the largest and longest debts first (at least the median overdue amount, 60 days or more), then a usually prompt customer late for the first time (3 or more settled invoices in 12 months, none late), then the rest; each by amount × days, then amount, then name. An invoice is due for a reminder when it is `first_after_days` (7) overdue with none sent, or its last reminder is more than `repeat_after_days` (14) old; the type is `type_first` for the first and `type_repeat` after (empty: the company's default). Never a reminder for a customer with a Dunning in draft, below `min_amount`, listed in `phone_only`, or whose payment record couldn't be read (`not_shown`, or beyond the 50 asked about; such a customer is ranked without the "usually prompt" step, and the notice says so). A truncated Dunning list leaves no cards that day.
- **Outputs:** one "Who to chase today" notice (up to 10 customers: amount, days, invoices, how they pay, reminders sent and due, the rank's rule, and a reason line each), and a Dunning card per (customer, invoice) due, in ranking order, at most 5 a day, deduped per invoice and Dunning Type, its fields `{sales_invoice, dunning_type, posting_date}` with the letter date from ERPNext's check. The card reuses the Dunning card's view and executor; only `asked_by` and `configured_by` come from the job.

### Payment checks (`watch.jobs.payment_checks`)

- **When:** every hour from 08:00 to 18:00, Monday to Friday, company time; at most 10 cards a day across the hours. Settings: `company`, `due_within_days` (14, 1–400), `block_submitted` (off).
- **Reads**, as listed in oe_connector: the company's unpaid Purchase Invoices due within `due_within_days`, drafts and submitted (`list_records`, `docstatus ["<", 2]`, `outstanding_amount [">", 0]`, `due_date ["<=", $date]`); the same suppliers' submitted invoices of the last 120 days (`supplier ["in", $parties]`, the 50 soonest due); and `supplier_bank_changed` for them. Both derived reads are skipped when nothing is due.
- **Duplicates** (code, the same rules oe_connector's block applies): the same supplier and currency, both with a supplier invoice date, and the same bill number once normalized (case, spaces, dashes, leading zeros), a real one, with the same amount or dates within 60 days (**high**); or the same amount and bill date (**medium**); or the same amount within 3 days (**low**, a notice only, never proposed). The copy is a draft against a submitted invoice, or the later posted of two submitted ones, unpaid and not already on hold.
- **A duplicate draft:** a hold card (`draft_update`: `on_hold` 1 and a `hold_comment` from code's template, "Possible duplicate of <other>: same bill number" or "… same amount and date", cleaned, at most 280 characters), only when ERPNext's check as the reviewer says the draft is theirs or assigned to them; otherwise a notice.
- **A duplicate submitted invoice:** a notice saying to use Block Invoice in ERPNext, or, with the job's `block_submitted`, `ERPNEXT_BLOCK_INVOICE` and the pinned `draft_block_invoice` all on, a block card (`integrations.erpnext_block`): `draft_check` with operation `block` and `{duplicate_of, release_date}` (the run's day plus 14), showing ERPNext's figures for both invoices, the payments under way and "held until someone unblocks it, at the latest <release date>".
- **A changed bank account** (changed after the last payment, or never paid with details from the last 30 days): a notice with code's own line, "Confirm the change with the supplier by phone, on a number you already have, before paying."
- **Approving a block** re-checks all three switches first (409 `block_off`, nothing claimed), separation of duties, and `{duplicate_of, release_date}` (after today, at most 90 days ahead). It sends `{name, duplicate_of, release_date, idempotency_key, asked_by: "job:payment-checks", configured_by, expected_fingerprint}`, only for the payment-checks job's card. A changed invoice, separation of duties, a blocking limit, an invoice a person unblocked before, or a block not from the job's card closes the card. `erpnext_changes.enabled("block")` lists nothing, so chat and ERPNext's panel can never propose one.

### Quote follow-up (`watch.jobs.quote_follow_up`)

- **When:** 07:30, Monday to Friday, company time; at most 5 cards a day. Settings: `company`, `days_ahead` (5, 1–30), `min_amount` (0) and `assign_to` (an ERPNext user; empty: the reviewer). No model is called.
- **Reads**, three, as listed in oe_connector: every submitted Quotation to a Customer valid until at least 7 days ago (`list_records`, `docstatus 1`, `quotation_to "Customer"`, `valid_till [">=", $date]`; `name, party_name, customer_name, transaction_date, valid_till, grand_total, currency, status, order_type, amended_from`, up to 500), one read because a shape holds neither a status list nor two bounds on one field; the same for quotations to a Lead (`quotation_to "Lead"`) with only `name, valid_till, grand_total, currency, status`, so no party, name or contact field of theirs is ever read (oe_connector refuses one); then read 1's customers' Sales Orders, drafts and submitted, since the oldest of their quotations (`customer ["in", $customers]`, the 50 most pressing; `name, customer, transaction_date, items.prevdoc_docname`), skipped when no quotation to a customer counts. Neither reads Lead, Contact, the sales team or Communication.
- **Rules** (code, tested on fixed data): **lapsing** is still open (Open, Replied or Partially Ordered) and valid until today or within `days_ahead`; **lapsed** is valid until 1 to 7 days ago and Expired (or still Open or Replied before ERPNext's daily expiry). Never a quotation below `min_amount`, one a Sales Order line names (it or the one it was amended from) whatever its status says, or one revised since: a revision counts once, as its latest. Lapsed first, then by value × closeness to lapsing, then name. A quotation to a Lead is counted from read 2, each row once (its `amended_from` isn't read), "N more to leads, not named.", and never named or carded; a cut read 2 is noted.
- **Outputs:** one "Quotations to follow up" notice (up to 10: the customer, quotation, value, date quoted, valid till, days left or "lapsed N days ago", status; notes when either read was cut), and a ToDo card per quotation to a customer (`allocated_to` the job's `assign_to`, else the reviewer's email; `reference_type` Quotation; `date` today, or the day before it lapses when later; `priority` High for the three largest, else Medium; `description` code's template only: "Call <customer> about <quotation> (<value>, valid till <date>): ask whether it's still wanted, and what would win it. If it's lapsed, offer to re-quote at today's prices.", the customer's name cleaned as a notice cleans it). A quotation whose orders couldn't all be read (its customer beyond the 50, an id the `$customers` slot wouldn't take, or the order list cut) gets no card, nor one whose name isn't its own clean; the currency shows only as three capitals. A quotation ERPNext won't let the reviewer prepare (their permissions) comes off the reviewer's notice and goes to the principal. Each is raised once while lapsing and once after it lapses (`once`, key `q:<name>:<lapsing|lapsed>`). `check_fields` takes exactly that ToDo: on a Quotation, High or Medium, the template naming that quotation (the customer its own clean, the name ERPNext's pattern and its own clean, the currency three capitals), assigned to the job's assignee now (a changed `assign_to` or reviewer refuses an older card), and `erpnext_drafts._todo`'s output unchanged. Re-quoting is the person's own chat turn, never the job's.

### Late deliveries (`watch.jobs.late_deliveries`)

- **When:** 07:15, Monday to Friday, company time; at most 5 cards a day. Settings: `company`, `min_days_late` (2, 1–60), `assign_to` (an ERPNext user; empty: the reviewer) and `skip_suppliers` (suppliers chased another way). No model is called.
- **Reads**, two, as listed in oe_connector: every submitted Purchase Order not fully received and due before today (`list_records`, `docstatus 1`, `per_received ["<", 100]`, `schedule_date ["<", $date]`; `name, supplier, status, transaction_date, schedule_date, per_received, grand_total, currency` and the lines' `items.item_code, items.qty, items.received_qty, items.schedule_date`, a row per order and line, up to 500); then the Supplier Delivery Record report for the company over the last 365 days (`run_report`, `company`, `from_date`, `to_date`; one row per supplier, no supplier filter, so one call for all), skipped when no order counts. A shape holds no status list, so code drops Closed, On Hold and Completed orders. Neither reads Contact, a supplier's bank details or anyone's hours, and nothing reads ToDo.
- **Rules** (code, tested on fixed data): a line is late when it received less than it ordered and was due before today; an order is as late as its oldest late line and counts from `min_days_late` days; never a supplier in `skip_suppliers`. Most days late first, then value, then name. A line's fields are read under their dotted key or ERPNext's bare one (a bare `schedule_date` is the line's). The supplier's record is code's words from the report's counts: "late on N of M lines in 12 months, X days on average", "on time on all M lines in 12 months", "no receipts in 12 months" (no row), or "not read this run" when the report was cut; a row whose counts don't read is left out.
- **Outputs:** one "Late deliveries" notice (up to 10: the supplier, order, days late, oldest due date, what's missing (up to three lines, then a count), value, status and the supplier's record; notes for more than 10 and for either read cut), and a ToDo card per late order (`allocated_to` the job's `assign_to`, else the reviewer's email, read again at each check; `reference_type` Purchase Order; `date` today; `priority` High when more than 7 days late, else Medium; `description` code's template only: "Chase <supplier> on <order>: <n> lines due <date>, <qty> of <item> [and <k> more lines] missing. Ask for a confirmed delivery date and update the order's schedule date. Their record: <record>.", the supplier's and item's names cleaned as a notice cleans them, until cleaning changes nothing). The chase note is text the buyer sends from their own mail; the job adds no mail path. No card when the order list was cut (an order's lines may be short), for a name that isn't ERPNext's pattern and its own clean, for text past the template's own bounds, or while an earlier week's card for the same order still waits. An order ERPNext won't let the reviewer prepare comes off the reviewer's notice and goes to the principal. Each order is raised once a week while late (`once`, key `po:<name>:<ISO week>`), so the card store's hold rules apply within the week. `check_fields` takes exactly that ToDo: on a Purchase Order, High or Medium, the template naming that order (the supplier and item their own clean, the record one of code's four forms), assigned to the job's assignee now, and `erpnext_drafts._todo`'s output unchanged.

### Bank matching (`watch.jobs.bank_matching`, `integrations.erpnext_match`)

- **When:** daily at 10:00, company time, after the morning's statement import and ERPNext's own hourly matching rules; at most 30 cards a day. Settings: `company`, `bank_accounts` (up to 10 Bank Account names, each also listed by an ERPNext operator in `oe_connector_bank_matching`, with no payroll on it), `amount_cap_day` (50,000 in the company's currency by default, 1 to 1,000,000). With no account set, the run leaves one notice saying to name them.
- **Reads:** `bank_lines_to_match {bank_account, from_date}` once per account (the last 60 days; oe_connector redacts account-like numbers in the bank's text and leaves out Employee and payroll lines); `bank_line_candidates {bank_transaction: $bank_line}` once per line still unallocated and at least a day old, oldest first, at most 50 a run (more are cut and the notice says so); and `list_records` for the unpaid Sales or Purchase Invoices of the parties of the lines nothing fits (skipped when there are none). oe_connector's listing names read 1 once per account, by its name (`bank_matching.listing`).
- **Rules** (code): a candidate counts only in the line's currency, dated on or before it, and never for another party than the line's. **High:** the same party and amount. **Medium:** the same amount, the line with no party (explicitly none: a missing key means "can't tell"), and the voucher's reference, 6 characters or more on word boundaries, in the bank's reference or description. **Low:** the same amount or party only: never proposed and never shown: a card holds only what ERPNext checked as the reviewer. A candidate carrying exactly the line's reference is left to ERPNext's own rules. One voucher a card, and only when exactly one fits at the best confidence.
- **Notices:** a likely match no card was left for; "Bank lines to match in ERPNext's Banking app" for two vouchers that fit equally, a partial payment, a payment with no voucher yet, or one payment for several of the party's unpaid invoices (the job never makes a voucher or matches a partial); "Bank lines with nothing to match"; and once a month, the matches approved the month before, from the job's own cards, to check against the bank statement.
- **The match card** (operation `match`, `draft_check {operation: "match", doctype: "Bank Transaction", name, fields: {vouchers: [{doctype, name}]}}`, with no amounts: ERPNext computes the allocation in a rolled-back savepoint): one to five Payment or Journal Entries, sorted, each named once (`erpnext_match.match_fields`, again at approval). The check as the reviewer must read back the line and its vouchers whole (a key the rules need missing leaves no card), the line in the company's currency, each voucher on the line's side of the account, dated on or before it, for its party, allocated and cleared in full, the line Reconciled after with its whole unallocated amount taken, and the reviewer neither the statement's importer nor a voucher's creator by email ("Administrator" never matches). A cleaned, capped slice of the summary (at most 5 vouchers and 20 creators, never the bank's text) is stored with the card. The card shows the line, each voucher's allocation and clearance date, the line after and who imported the statement.
- **Approval** re-checks `ERPNEXT_BANK_MATCH` and the pin (409 `match_off`, nothing claimed), the job on, separation of duties by person id, and from the stored slice the whole match, the card's own vouchers, and the approver's current email against the importer and creators (a match closes the card as `sod_refused`). Holding the claim, the job's day cap: what was approved of the job's cards today, by anyone, plus this one stays within `amount_cap_day` (`total_company_currency`), counted at the claim in one transaction, once per card, failing closed; over it the claim is released and the card waits (409 `match_limit`, "today's matching limit is reached"). It sends `{name, vouchers, idempotency_key, asked_by: "job:bank-matching", configured_by, expected_fingerprint}`, a fixed set with no doctype, only for the bank-matching job's card. oe_connector rebuilds the card under lock against its fingerprint, then checks its own separation of duties and caps. A changed line or voucher, separation of duties, ERPNext's own matching limit, a line already reconciled, or a match not from the job's card closes the card; the next day's run proposes again. `erpnext_changes.enabled("match")` lists nothing, so chat and ERPNext's panel can never propose one.

### Invoice capture (`watch.jobs.invoice_capture`, `integrations.erpnext_fill`)

- **When:** working days at 09:00, 11:00, 13:00 and 15:00, company time (four slots sharing the day's caps), so a morning mail is filled by lunch. Settings: the company, `days_back` (14, at most 60), `amount_cap_day` (50,000 by default, at most 1,000,000), 30 cards a day. Runs as its own ERP user (`as_job_user`): oe_connector refuses the capture tools otherwise. When configuring the job, an ERPNext operator limits its ERP user (`oe-watch-invoice-capture@<site>`) to exactly one Company by User Permission, applying to all DocTypes; without that, oe_connector refuses every mailed-draft read.
- **Reads:** (1) `mail_invoices_to_fill` (the drafts a supplier's mail made, with the mail's own From as it arrived, the account's DMARC statement, the From domain's published policy, the supplier its Contacts name, the one attachment and the assignees); (2) `read_attachment` once per fillable draft (`$mail_draft`, `$mail_file`), at most 20 a run, `may_fail`; (3) and (4) `list_records` of the suppliers' submitted, not fully billed Purchase Orders and Receipts; (5) the company's currency. The first two are withheld from chat and open only to this job's read marker.
- **The sender gate** (`erpnext_fill.fill_allowed`, the owner's, Nov 11, 2026): `sender_checked` is "dmarc-enforced", `sender_from` is set, and `sender_policy` is "reject", or "quarantine" with the account's `authserv_id` check passed; any missing key fails. oe_connector refuses the same cases. A draft that fails it gets a "can't be filled from here" line with the reason; its PDF is never read.
- **What it bills, code only:** only oe_connector's deterministic fields of the PDF are used (invoice number, date, totals, currencies, Purchase Order references); its text never reaches a model and the job has no reason step. The one Purchase Order the PDF names, when the job may open it and it is the supplier's and still open; else, when it names none, the one open Purchase Receipt of the supplier at the PDF's total to the cent in the company's currency. Dates: ISO, D/M/Y or M/D/Y only when a part is above 12, and month names; an ambiguous date, no number, no single total, no text layer, another currency, two orders, a closed or someone else's order, or no or several receipts at the total is "a person fills these".
- **The fill card** (operation `fill`, `draft_fill_purchase_invoice`): `{source, lower: [], bill_no, bill_date}`; no row is lowered in v1. ERPNext's check, as the reviewer, must read back the job's company, supplier and From, pass the gate, no other invoice with that bill number, the company's currency (`check_fill_currency`), the PDF's total (`check_fill_total`), the reviewer the draft's assignee (`check_fill_assignee`: only the person the mail pull assigned the draft to approves, never a self-assignment; the reviewer is told an ERPNext operator points the Purchase Invoice assignment rule at them, or the draft is filled by hand) and no creator of the source (`check_fill_sod`, told to the principal). The card shows the PDF's own number, date and total beside ERPNext's fill. Off unless `ERPNEXT_INVOICE_FILL` and the pin hold, checked again at approval with the gate, the assignee and separation of duties on the stored slice, then the job's day cap at the claim (what was approved of the job's cards today, by anyone). It sends `{name, source, lower, bill_no, bill_date, idempotency_key, asked_by: "job:invoice-capture", configured_by, expected_fingerprint}`, no doctype. A changed draft or source, a bill number in use, not the assignee, the gate, an already filled draft or not the job's card closes the card. The draft stays a draft: nothing is submitted, paid or posted.
- **Each month,** to the principal (`to_principal`): the fills approved the month before, and any tried but never confirmed, to check before they are submitted.
